blocks.text: Abstract

Large language model agents solve tasks by generating trajectories that interleave planning, tool calls, and intermediate results. Current evaluation metrics reduce such a trajectory to a binary success flag or compare it against a reference by exact matching. A success flag cannot distinguish a sound solution from one that succeeds by luck, and says nothing about why a failed run went wrong. Exact matching penalizes plans that are valid but reordered or decomposed differently from the reference. We reframe trajectory evaluation as a distance between the agent’s execution graph and a set of valid solution graphs, and instantiate it via an unbalanced fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport problem over attributed dependency graphs. The resulting score, termedOtap(Optimal Transport for Agentic Planning), is a pseudo-metric that is provably invariant to dependency-preserving reorderings and has bounded sensitivity to redundant steps. Its unbalancedmarginalshandlemissingorhallucinatedstepswithout forcing a match, and its soft coupling accommodates variationinplangranularity.Oncontrolledperturbationsandthree public benchmarks,Otapseparates valid from invalid trajectories in a regime where semantics-only metrics score below chance. Its accuracy is highest when the dependency graph is recovered exactly, and drops only when the graph is inferred heuristically from free-text traces.

blocks.text: Related Work

Agent benchmarks.Existing evaluation suites like Agent- Bench (Liu et al. 2024), GAIA (Mialon et al. 2024), WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024), ToolBench (Qin et al. 2024), and τ-bench (Yao et al. 2024) primarily emphasize environmental task execution. PlanBench (Valmeekam et al. 2023) utilizes formal verification to assess planning accuracy, which provides exact ground truth but remains restricted to highly structured deterministic domains. These benchmarks do not offer a graded, open-ended distance metric between structural execution graphs. Some recent papers propose metricsbeyondaccuracytomeasureagentperformance,suchas confidencecalibration(Zhang,Xiong,andWu2026),uncertainty quantification (Tayebati et al. 2026), and consistency measurement (Raj et al. 2026).

However, PRMs require extensive step-level manual annotations and act as black-box learned models. Similarly, LLM-as-a-judge methods(Zhengetal.2023)inherithighinferencecostsand non-deterministic variations. In contrast,Otapis deterministic given text embeddings, is computationally lightweight, and provides explicit sub-loss decompositions. Text and structure similarity.Output level lexical metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) and semantic metrics (Raj, Rosati, and Majumdar 2023; Zhang et al. 2020) alike fail to model trajectory-levelnuancessuchascausaldependencies,macrolevel plan structure, or tool environments. Classical graph matchers such as Graph Edit Distance (GED) (Sanfeliu and Fu 1983) do capture topological structure, but are generally NP-hard and lack the capacity to incorporate soft, highdimensional semantic vector spaces over node attributes. Optimal transport.Optimal transport provides a mathematical foundation for aligning probability distributions (Peyré and Cuturi 2019). Problem Formulation

Definition 1(Trajectory graph).An agent execution trajectory is represented as an attributed directed acyclic graph G= (V, E, ϕ),whereeachvertexsi ∈Vdefinesanexecuted step: si = (ai, τi, ci, ei), comprising an action descriptionai, an invoked tool identifierτ i ∈ T(whereτ i =∅denotes an internal reasoning step), specific contextual argumentsci, and an execution effect or post-state artifactei. A directed edge(si, sk)∈E indicates a strict data or causal dependency where stepsk consumes an artifact or requires the prior execution of step si.Themappingfunctionϕprojectsstepfieldsintoacontinuous vector space. Edges are systematically constructed via three mechanisms: (a) extracting explicit dependency graphs from planand-execute planners; (b) tracing artifact dependencies in ReAct sequences by linking actions to recent observations; or(c)revertingconservativelytoatotalexecutionorderwhen structural dependencies are unrecoverable. TheOtapMetric

We now formalize Optimal Transport Agent Plan (Otap) to quantify the similarity between am agent trajectoryPand a reference setR. Instead of treating agent trajectories as flat text strings or relying on binary success criteria,Otap modelsexecutionhistoriesasdirectedacyclicgraphs(DAGs) capturingbothsemanticcontentandexecutiondependencies.

Experiments

We evaluateOtapby comparing it with a range of metrics (lexical, semantic, and graph-based) in a diverse set of tasks. We hand curate a set of realistic and challenging agentic tasks, as well as use three public benchmarks: PlanBench (Valmeekam et al. 2023), WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024), and GAIA (Mialon et al. 2024). The perturbations are:(P1)synonym-level paraphrase of all step texts;(P2)an alternative linear extension of the same DAG; (P3)merge of two dependent adjacent steps, or split of a compound step into two chained sub-steps;(P4)causal inversion: swapping two steps across a dependency edge, so the consumer executes before its producer;(P5)corruption: deletionofacriticalstep,insertionof1-3irrelevantdistractor steps, incompatible tool swaps, or combinations. Agent-side graphs are re-extracted from the perturbed sequences by artifact tracing, so a P4 inversion manifests exactly as it would in a real trace: an unsatisfiable dependency. Ground truth places the original and P1–P3 in one validity tier, P4 strictly below, and P5 at the bottom. blocks.text: Benchmark evaluations

The controlled corpus establishes internal validity; we now test transfer on three public benchmarks that differ deliberately in how much trust each places in the dependency structure and in the labels. PlanBench (real LLM plans, oracle labels).The Plan- Bench release (Valmeekam et al. 2023) ships blocksworld plans generated by real LLMs together with VAL-checked validity flags. We convert each LLM plan and the gold plan into trajectory graphs usingexactproduces/consumes sets from the PDDL operator semantics—dependency DAGs are ground truth here, not heuristic (mechanism (a) of Sec. 3)— and buildK=3genuinely distinctvalidreferences per instance with an exact solver (gold plan, an alternative optimum under a different tie-break, and a state-preserving detour variant). We sample60plans per model (balanced across valid/invalid where possible) for12models spanning GPT-3.5/4/4o, Claude 3/3.5, Gemini, Llama-3.1, and Qwen families:720real trajectories. Our re-implemented validity checker agrees with the shipped VAL labels on720/720 plans. Two studies result: (a) anoracle study—per-metric AUROC of the score against the validity label, the “external checkatzeroannotationcost”;and(b)theP1–P5/Q1–Q5protocol run on20gold plans (520trajectories), i.e. controlled ground truth overreal-domainplans with exact dependency semantics. Cost is not flat in trajectory length: on GAIA’s longer humanauthored solutions the quadratic Gromov–Wasserstein term raises the mean to23.9s per evaluation (ROUGE-L’s LCS suffers similarly, at180s), consistent with the complexity analysis of Sec. 5; sparse structural distances and earlystopped outer iterations are the natural mitigations for longhorizon traces. In the short-horizon regimeOtapremains negligible next to an LLM-judge call, which costs seconds oflatencyandper-tokenfeesandisnon-deterministic;Otap is deterministic, offline, and cheap enough to run inside a training loop as a process reward.
Human evaluation
Validatingametricrequirestrajectorieswhoserelativequal-
ity is known. Our evidence therefore comes in two tiers.
Thefirstisafullyautomatic,reproducibleprotocolinwhich

ground-truth quality orderings holdby construction: a corpus of plan DAGs is subjected to controlled perturbations of known severity, and a metric is measured by how often it recovers the resulting ordering (Part A) and by its correlation with a graded corruption ladder (Part B). The second tier moves to three public benchmarks: PlanBench, where 720real LLM-generated planscarry oracle validity labels at zero annotation cost; and GAIA and WebArena, where the perturbation protocol is re-run on real human-authored solutions and real task intents, respectively. Across all studies (3,092trajectories in total) we use a single fixed seed and thea prioridefault hyper-parameters of Sec. 4; no tuning of any kind was performed on any corpus. We release the full harness—corpora, loaders, perturbation generator, all metric implementations, and seeds—for one-command reproduction.
Conclusion

In this paper, we have proposedOtapas a granular metric for evaluating agent trajectories that account for their heterogenous graph structure and multiple reference solutions. Beyond evaluation, the differentiable structure of (3) makes Otapa candidate dense process reward, and the soft-min overreferencespointstowardlearnedmodelsofthesolution manifold.Theexperimentsrevealtwoopenproblemsthatwe leave for future work: dependency extraction from free-text traces, and principled granularity invariance.
